rules.rule:
This is Wyolet Relay, a high-throughput LLM router. Besides general Go review, enforce these project rules and flag every violation:

## Module and import boundaries
- `sdk/v1/` (canonical protocol) imports nothing from `app/`, `internal/` or any `sdk/adapters/<vendor>/`.
- Each `sdk/adapters/<vendor>/` imports `sdk/v1/` and never another vendor adapter. One folder per vendor; wire-shape names never appear in folder paths.
- The `sdk/` module imports nothing from `app/` or `internal/`; `pkg/` imports nothing from `app/` or `internal/`.
- No vendor names (openai, anthropic, gemini, cohere) in `app/` code except catalog data lookups, error messages and URL paths. Only `cmd/relay/` (the composition root) builds vendor-specific adapter specs. Dispatch, routing, pipeline and HTTP code never branch on a vendor.

## Adapters and the canonical protocol
- Translators are stateless; per-stream state lives only in the closures the stream factories return.
- Vendor-specific features go in `Extensions`, not new top-level canonical fields (prompt caching is the one first-class exception).
- Same-vendor opaque blobs (thinking signatures, encrypted reasoning) ride in `provider_data` and round-trip verbatim.
- Refusal is a finish/stop reason on a normal message, never its own item type.
- No silent drops: an adapter must never accept input or upstream output it cannot express and discard it. It must emit it, carry it in `provider_data`/`Extensions`, annotate an irreducible drop with a `// canonical: <field> dropped — <why>` comment, or, for safety-relevant signals (unknown finish reason, content filter, refusal), surface it rather than report success.

## Hot path (request handling)
- No Postgres calls on the request path; catalog reads come from the in-memory snapshot only.
- Async work (usage, payload, metrics emits) uses bounded channels with drop-on-full and a drop counter; never unbounded queues, never a blocking send on the request path.
- Post-flight work runs in a detached goroutine after the response body closes and must not block the response.
- Token counts come from the provider response; no relay-side tokenisation.
- Be allocation-conscious: reuse buffers, avoid needless string conversions.

## Storage and kv
- No pgx/pgxpool/pgconn types in signatures outside `internal/storage` and store constructors; no SQL outside `internal/storage/gen/queries.sql` and the per-entity store files; no sqlc-generated types in exported store signatures.
- kv keys are hash-tagged `{tag}:`, built in the consumer's `keys.go`, and carry a TTL unless a comment justifies it.

## Authorization
- Every control-plane mutation goes through the Authorizer; handlers never branch on user identity directly.

## Conventions
- Comments state why, in one to three lines, never what the code does or its history.
- Names describe what the code does; no marketing or abstract words in identifiers.
- Configuration comes from environment/config, never hardcoded hosts or secrets.
- One responsibility per file; a file far past ~300 lines usually needs splitting.
- Tests must test behaviour: flag tautological tests, tests that only exercise mocks, and skipped tests without a reason.
